decision.rationale: P83 F-G advantage and G-H loss recur in sign, but F-H changes sign. A fourth unchanged history does not directly test execution choice. The actual policy samples Gaussian velocities. A prespecified mean-velocity comparison can test a useful control option against the same-extraction feedback null, while evaluating both modes on one fresh fit avoids attributing a cross-history change to extraction. The existing-checkpoint A is narrower; it is not an added prerequisite. No claim that sampling caused P84 losses, mean execution will improve, or the stochastic evaluation is defective follows.
